results.title: Brain region identification
results.question: What are the major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body?
results.response: The major subdivisions of the Drosophila mushroom body are the calyx, pedunculus, and mushroom body lobe system. This information comes from the VFB database, which states that the mushroom body is divided into these three parts: the calyx, which receives sensory interneuron afferents, the pedunculus, a thick axon bundle extending from the calyx to the base of the lobes, and the mushroom body lobe system, consisting of a vertical branch and a medial branch.

results.title: Complete neuron profile
results.question: Give me a comprehensive profile of the giant fiber neuron: its anatomy, connectivity, available driver lines, and relevant publications.
results.response:
The [giant fiber neuron](https://www.virtualflybrain.org/reports/FBbt_00004020 "Open giant fiber neuron in Virtual Fly Brain") is a large adult descending neuron that controls jump escape behavior, as described by Thomas and Wyman (1984). According to VFB, it has a distinct anatomy and connectivity. The giant fiber neuron has a large descending axon and arborizes in the ipsilateral zones A and B of the antennal mechanosensory and motor center. There is one of these cells per hemisphere, and its large cell body is located posterior to the lower protocerebrum, as identified by Koto et al. (1981) and Namiki et al. (2018). The large descending axon of the giant fiber neuron is several times larger than any other axon in the cervical connective, as noted by Power (1948) and Koto et al. (1981). 

VFB holds extensive data on the giant fiber neuron, including [22](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,ListAllAvailableImages "Run in VFB: List all available images of DNp01") available images of DNp01, [14](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,TransgeneExpressionHere "Run in VFB: Transgene expression in DNp01") records of transgene expression in DNp01, [361](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,DownstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Downstream connectivity classes for DNp01") downstream connectivity classes, and [435](https://v2.virtualflybrain.org/org.geppetto.frontend/geppetto?q=FBbt_00004020,UpstreamClassConnectivity "Run in VFB: Upstream connectivity classes for DNp01") upstream connectivity classes. Additionally, VFB provides information on available driver lines, such as P{VT046265-GAL4} expression pattern. Relevant publications for the giant fiber neuron include those by Thomas and Wyman (1984), Koto et al. (1981), Namiki et al. (2018), and Sturner et al. (2025). 

The giant fiber neuron can be identified by its large descending axon, and its specific anatomy, connectivity, and available driver lines make it a well-studied neuron in Drosophila neuroscience. Further information on the giant fiber neuron can be found in the relevant publications and VFB data, including its role in jump escape behavior and its connectivity patterns.
